sentences.text:
Proceeding Sheet vs Amarnath on 2 April, 2026
 High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravathi
 C.C.No.4254 of 2025

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravathi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Proceeding Sheet
Sl. Office
 Order
No DATE Note 3. 02.04.2026 GRKP, J Heard Sri G.R. Sudhakar, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Sri V. Vinod K Reddy, learned Counsel for the Contempt Petitioner and Sri B. Ramesh, learned

Counsel appearing on behalf of Ms.
Y. Sushma, learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 & 2.
2.

Sri G.R. Sudhakar, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Sri V. Vinod K Reddy, learned Counsel for the Contempt Petitioner has drawn the attention of this Court to the Order passed by this Court dated 19.06.2025 in W.P.No.6792 of 2024 & Batch.
The operative portion of Para No.11 of the said Order would indicate that the Respondents were given 12 weeks time to pay the compensation.

The said paragraph would also indicate that the claimants who were similarly situated have approached this Court by filing W.P.No.22879 of 2018, in which this Court had directed the Respondent Authorities to pay the compensation as per the market value as per the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The present Contempt Case has been filed for non-compliance of the Order of the Court dated 19.06.2025 after completion of 12 weeks time that was granted for compliance.
The Contempt Case is filed on 29.12.2025 and the facts would also indicate that the Writ Appeal was filed on 31.01.2026 challenging the Order of this Court.
On a query of this Court, it is informed by both the Counsel that no Interim Order was passed by the Hon'ble Division Bench.

4. From the above facts, prima-facie, it appears to the Court that the Respondents have filed Writ Appeal on 31.01.2026 only after the Contempt Case had been filed one month before the said date i.e., on 29.12.2025.

The conduct of the Respondents/Contemnors, as mentioned above, prima-facie,
appears to be that Writ Appeal has been filed only to escape the consequences that would follow in the Contempt Proceedings and also to further delay the execution of the Order of this Court.
The Hon'ble Apex Court had dealt with similar situation in Israr Ahmad Khan Vs. Amarnath Prasad and Others : 2026 SCC OnLine SC 322.

entities.text: Israr Ahmad Khan Vs. Amarnath Prasad and Others : 2026 SCC OnLine SC 322
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraphs are usefully extracted hereunder:
"27.
Delayed filing of appeals should be the exception, but in recent times, the exception has practically evolved to become the rule.
Orders passed by the Courts are not complied with for a long time, and when Contempt Petitions are filed, belated appeals, with tremendous delay, are preferred.
Proceeding Sheet vs Amarnath on 2 April, 2026

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111768131/
1 28.

The (alleged) continuing contumacious conduct of the defaulting party is sought to be justified on the mere production of a Diary/Filing/Stamp Reporting Number showing that an appeal has been preferred, so as to obtain multiple adjournments in contempt matters.
29. We, in no uncertain terms, deprecate these practices.

It is felt that by such modus operandi, disobedient litigants act brazenly which has the further effect of bringing down the authority and majesty of the Courts and the rule of law, interfering in the administration of justice.
The same may well, in certain situations, border on criminal contempt.
30. The High Courts should deal with such unscrupulous litigants, moreso when they happen to be 'State', within the meaning of Article 12 of the Constitution, or like bodies, with an iron hand.

Unless the High Courts, so also this Court deal with these aspects firmly, we run the clear risk of erosion of the unflinching faith that the ordinary litigants of this country repose in the Judiciary at all levels.
It is the solemn duty of all of us manning the Courts across the hierarchy to ensure that the public faith never wavers.
5. In this view of the matter, issue Form-I Notice to the Contemnors/Respondent Nos.1 to 3.

Since the Contemnors/Respondent Nos.1 to 3 are already represented through the Counsel viz., Ms. Y.
Sushma, this Court deems it appropriate to dispense with the usual mode of notice.

Instead, learned Counsel for the Petitioner is directed to take out urgent Personal Notice in respect of Contemnors/Respondent Nos.1 to 3 within three days from today and file proof of receipt of notice within three days thereafter.

6. Sri B. Ramesh, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Ms. Y. Sushma, learned Counsel for the Respondent Nos.1 & 2 is not only directed to convey the gist of this Order but also communicate a copy of this Order to the Respondents forthwith for effective compliance.
6. List the matter on 22.04.2026.
